name: MN-04
label: Safe D

key_factors: D+18 district lean with long-serving incumbent Betty McCollum
Massive fundraising gap: $1.25M vs $28K, challenger nearly no cash
Prediction markets price Democratic win at ~95%
No polling or expert ratings, so uncertainty stays elevated
model.rationale: McCollum combines a strong D+18 district, incumbency, and an overwhelming money advantage against a barely funded challenger, and markets price her near-certain to win. With no polls available, the forecast stays anchored to fundamentals at a Safe D margin near 24 points.
model.watch: Any late polling showing an unusually tight race or a major outside spending surge for the challenger would be the first sign of movement.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Betty McCollum seeks another term in a St. Paul-area district that leans Democratic by 18 points. She has raised about $1.25 million and holds nearly $500,000 on hand, while Republican Paul Wikstrom has raised under $30,000 with almost no cash remaining and no outside support on either side. No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, but prediction markets put McCollum's chances around 95 percent.

The fundamentals point firmly to McCollum: the district lean, her incumbency advantage, and the lopsided money race all favor her, and the recent political environment adds a modest Democratic tailwind. The main source of uncertainty is simply the absence of polling, which keeps the margin estimate somewhat loose even though the outcome is very likely to be a comfortable McCollum victory.
